lesson.title: Classification capstone
lesson.summary: Produce a conditional classification conclusion that survives changed purpose, influence and profiling facts.

prerequisites.reason: One closing case needs a complete product-route assessment.
One closing case needs separation of learning and recruitment functions.
A contrasting closing case uses the creditworthiness listed-use boundary.
The closing cases require a reasoned paragraph 3 conclusion and supporting evidence.

blocks: **Classification capstone**: Northbridge's applicant platform first converts files and later adds personal suitability predictions. Assume the evaluation function is an AI system within scope and matches Annex III recruitment.
Those stipulated facts isolate the remaining test. Record which facts are established and which are assumptions; in a real decision obtain their evidence.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 2, 3(12), 3(52), 5, 6, 49, 111, 113; Annexes I and III

blocks: For the evaluative function, inspect paragraph 3's gateway, candidate condition and personal profiling. Personal suitability predictions support a profiling fact, which keeps the Annex III system high-risk despite a preparatory label.

For a separate formatting-only function, do not copy that result blindly; inspect its own system boundary, listed-purpose facts, errors and influence. Equally, do not copy its narrower result to the evaluator.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 2, 3(12), 3(52), 5, 6, 49, 111, 113; Annexes I and III

blocks: Changed case: the evaluator also performs a potentially prohibited practice. Classification is not a cure; investigate Article 5's complete test. Changed case: a new safety-product function is added. Check Article 6(1) separately.
A maintainable conclusion says which route and purpose it addresses. It avoids one immutable platform-wide label.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 2, 3(12), 3(52), 5, 6, 49, 111, 113; Annexes I and III

blocks: The final packet records evidence, source baseline, actors, scope, prohibition findings, both classification routes, paragraph 3/profiling, records, relevant duties and their dates. Explain unresolved facts.

This completes the classification reasoning exercise, not every high-risk compliance obligation. The later course programme covers those requirements. A defensible assessment states its limits rather than pretending the whole Act has been satisfied.
